accounting.rationale: R401 supplies a nonempty comma list and R402 the entity-name production; the complete502-head scan found no explicit entity-name rule. Actual eligibility remains C857: a variable or procedure pointer, not every named entity.
Normative statement-to-attribute definition, not a new S effect. PROTECTED usage restrictions, module/descendant exceptions and subobject inheritance retain8.5.15 ownership.
This is an attribute-specification route under8.5.1p1. C856 requires the specification part of a module, and C815 prevents a second explicit specification of the same attribute in one scoping unit.

PROTECTED is not PRIVATE. It distinguishes restrictions on nonpointer definition from restrictions on pointer association, with the actual8.5.15 exceptions; it does not freeze all target values or make every entity inaccessible.

The actual listed entities acquire the property. C857 admits variables and procedure pointers and C858 excludes common-block entities. Subobjects follow8.5.15p3, not an invented component-designator alternative in this name list.

PENDING finite8.5.15/19.6.7/19.6.8 and module/use/host relations. No read-only memory, thread synchronization, target-lifetime extension, case link, SourceUses approval or no-op runtime witness follows from the statement alone.

requirements.title: A PROTECTED statement requires a list of eligible entity names
requirements.definition: PROTECTED is followed by an optional double colon and a nonempty comma-separated entity-name list. R401 and the assumed R402 supply the list and names. A name may identify an eligible variable or procedure pointer, but the syntax contains no array/coarray declarator, component reference or invocation. The statement must obey module-specification, eligibility, common-block and single-attribute constraints; the operative protection rules are those of8.5.15.

pending.double-colon-form: PENDING complete module with an ordinary explicitly typed INTEGER variable value and PROTECTED :: value in its specification part. No PROTECTED type attribute, COMMON, initialization or executable definition is added.
pending.no-double-colon-form: PENDING the same complete declaration using PROTECTED value. Both colons are absent; the variable and module context remain unchanged.
pending.multiple-module-data: PENDING two distinct ordinary module variables in one PROTECTED name list, each explicitly typed and not already PROTECTED. Include a separate one-comma list repair if grammar reporting is tested; do not replace a separator defect with a duplicate-attribute or undeclared-name failure.
pending.mixed-variable-procedure-pointer: PENDING a complete module with ordinary INTEGER data and a real procedure-pointer entity specified through a valid explicit-interface PROCEDURE(...), POINTER declaration, followed by one PROTECTED statement listing both. The template and EXTERNAL property must be valid. A nonpointer procedure, abstract-interface name or named constant is not an equivalent entity; no unassociated invocation is made.
pending.missing-list-exclusion: PENDING complete bare and double-colon empty-list negatives in an otherwise valid module specification part, repaired solely by inserting one existing eligible variable name with required spacing. Diagnose the actual missing required list in the fixed source context, not a generic EOF, nonmodule placement, unsupported attribute or unrelated declaration.
pending.name-not-declarator: PENDING an already declared ordinary array variable a and PROTECTED :: a(:), repaired to PROTECTED :: a. The repair retains the same whole eligible module variable. Component/coarray/invocation contrasts need independent source-isolated repairs, not automatic credit for deleting arbitrary suffixes.
pending.eligibility-and-scope-source: PENDING finite relations to C856 module-only specification, C857 variable/procedure-pointer eligibility and C858 common-block exclusion. A submodule's permission to define an already protected ancestor entity is not permission to give a new entity PROTECTED in the submodule. Nonmodule or wrong-entity negatives retain their canonical owners.
pending.single-specification-source: PENDING C815 relations for a single PROTECTED statement versus a type/procedure PROTECTED attribute plus another explicit statement. Actual host/use identity and accessibility must be preserved; keyword absence or a similarly spelled local name is not proof of a different attribute state.
pending.protected-use-context-source: PENDING source/case relationships to C859/C860,8.5.15p2,19.6.7 and19.6.8, preserving actual use association, pointer versus nonpointer subject, definition versus association context and defining-module/descendant exceptions. PRIVATE accessibility and target-value mutation are not interchangeable with PROTECTED restrictions.
pending.subobject-and-pointer-state-source: PENDING finite8.5.15p2/p3 and19.5.2 relations for actual subobjects and the permitted undefined-association exceptions when a target is lost through another route or a specified completion event. Declaration does not extend target lifetime, prohibit every target write or initialize an association status. Do not query a pointer after its status becomes undefined or invent a mandatory runtime trap.

requirements.oracle: Complete standalone-statement compile admissions and source-isolated name/list repairs in a legitimate module specification part. Attribute restrictions and effects retain their canonical owners; a property declaration does not itself execute a protected operation.
requirements.oracle_limitation: Required syntax reporting does not prescribe fatal rejection, particular English or a printed R858. Wrong scope/entity, duplicate attributes, COMMON membership, missing procedure interfaces, unsupported PROTECTED, quoted/context-only records, wrong origins and native failures are not independent grammar witnesses. No association, target-value, subobject, access-control or runtime-effect approval is created.
